business_scope.primary_industry_name: Open-Market Brokerage of Solid-State Drives and Server Processors

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (National Unitary Jurisdiction; registered seat to be established in a canton such as Zurich or Zug; no sub-state tax distinction at federal level)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law — Germanico-Romanistic codified doctrine under the Swiss Civil Code (ZGB, SR 210) and the Code of Obligations (OR, SR 220), supplemented by federal administrative and regulatory law; not a Common Law jurisdiction
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Free Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China (signed 6 July 2013, in force 1 July 2014) — tariff concessions relevant to wholesale of electronics (ISIC 4651)
EFTA Convention (Vaduz, 21 June 2001, as amended 4 July 2014) — free movement of goods with Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway

Switzerland–EU Bilateral Agreements I and II (including the 1972 Free Trade Agreement and the 2009 Agreement on Customs Facilitation and Security) — market access and trade facilitation for semiconductors
Double Taxation Agreement between Switzerland and the United States (signed 2 October 1996, effective 1 January 1998; revised protocol 2019 on information exchange)
Double Taxation Agreement between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China (signed 6 December 2013, in force 10 October 2014)
Bilateral Investment Treaty between Switzerland and Hong Kong SAR (in force 11 December 1994)
Bilateral Investment Treaty between Switzerland and Singapore (in force 17 June 1978; amended 24 July 2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: SR 955.0 — Bundesgesetz über die Bekämpfung der Geldwäscherei und der Terrorismusfinanzierung (Anti-Money Laundering Act, AMLA) of 10 October 1997, as revised by the Federal Act of 22 December 2023 (in force 1 October 2024), Art. 2 para. 1 let. a, Art. 3 (beneficial-owner definition), Art. 8a to 8j (identity verification and central UBO register); SR 955.01 — Geldwäschereiverordnung (AMLO) of 22 December 1999; SR 955.033.0 — FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA) of 12 January 2006; SR 221.214.111 — Handelsregisterverordnung (Commercial Register Ordinance, HRA) of 17 October 2007, Art. 55 to 60 (firm-name rules); SR 210 — Civil Code (ZGB), Art. 52 to 59 (legal personality and organs); SR 220 — Code of Obligations (OR), Art. 552 to 827 (Aktiengesellschaft), Art. 950 to 960 (firm-name, truthfulness and public-authority name protection); SR 946.231 — Bundesgesetz über das Verbot der Finanzierung von Massenvernichtungswaffen (Embargo Act) and SECO sanctions ordinances (e.g., Russia Ordinance SR 946.231.169.7); SR 211.221.431 — implementing legislation of the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the Swiss central UBO register (Vedutenregister) established under revised AMLA Art. 9j et seq. is not publicly searchable; access is restricted to competent authorities (Federal Department of Finance, FINMA, SECO, cantonal tax and prosecution authorities), to financial intermediaries and DNFBPs subject to AML duties, and to Swiss banks conducting statutory customer due diligence; the register records name, date of birth, nationality and residence of each beneficial owner but not full identification numbers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified colour copy of passport or national identity card of each UBO, director and authorized signatory (Passkopie / Copie certifiée)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal civil-law notary public (Civil Law Notariat) or the competent cantonal passport authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille — Switzerland is a contracting party to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961; documents from non-Hague states must undergo consular legalization through the competent Swiss embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and official excerpt from the foreign corporate register for each corporate UBO (Handelsregisterauszug / Extracto del registro)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or Companies House of the UBO's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent foreign authority or consular legalization by the Swiss diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation of the Swiss AG (öffentliche Beurkundung der Statuten / Acte notarié d'incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss civil-law notary in the canton of the registered office (Cantonal Notariat)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille not required for domestic Swiss recognition; for foreign counterparties, apostille is issued by the competent Cantonal State Chancellery

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's certificate verifying the paid-up share capital (Liberierungsbescheinigung / Attestation de libération) and bank reference letter from the Swiss bank of the company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or private bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille not required for Swiss domestic use; the banker's signature is certified under bank signature protocol and accepted by the Commercial Register Office

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, shareholders and material trading counterparties against the following lists prior to incorporation and on a continuous real-time basis thereafter: (1) FINMA AMLO-FINMA annex including politically exposed persons (PEPs) of Swiss and foreign public administrations; (2) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions schedules as implemented by the Swiss Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO sanction ordinances, including the Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, North Korea and Venezuela regimes; (3) SECO State Secretariat for Economic Affairs sanctions list; (4) OFAC SDN list — applied as contractual best practice by Swiss banks for USD Swift_TT payment rails; (5) consolidated EU sanctions lists as cross-reference. Screening algorithm: fuzzy matching at 85% similarity threshold, human review of all alerts, enhanced due diligence (EDD) mandatory for PEPs, for UBOs in high-risk third states and for counterparties using escrow-inspection wire structures; negative news and adverse media check required for each applicant, with results archived for at least 10 years per AMLA documentation duties.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun: All foreign-issued identity, corporate and good-standing documents must bear an apostille or consular legalization dated within 90 days of submission; documents in languages other than German, French, Italian or English require a sworn translation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex / Central Business Names Index) — the official federal search and filing portal operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt / Office fédéral du registre du commerce) of the Federal Department of Justice and Police; incorporation filings are made through the cantonal commercial register office competent for the registered seat (e.g., the Zurich Handelsregisteramt or the Zug Handelsregisteramt), using canton-specific e-portals integrated with Zefix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 950 para. 1 OR, the company name must be composed in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh) and must satisfy the principles of truthfulness, distinctiveness and non-misleading character (Art. 950 para. 2 OR; Art. 940 para. 2 OR). A Latin-script transliteration is mandatory; Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese or other non-Latin characters are not admissible as the registered principal name. The legal-form suffix 'AG' or 'SA' (or, in permitted cases, 'Ltd.') must be appended to the firm name. An additional foreign-language trade name (Zusatz) is permissible provided it is truthful, not misleading, and the Swiss legal-form suffix is retained. The declared business purpose — open-market brokerage of solid-state drives and server processors (ISIC 4651) — must be consistent with the chosen name so that the name does not create a false impression as to the actual object of the enterprise.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca — requires prior FINMA banking license and express approval by the supervisory authority
Insurance / Assurances / Versicherung — requires prior FINMA authorization
Trust / Treuhand — requires a fiduciary license or SRO membership under AMLO in certain cantons and may trigger enhanced commercial-register review

Swiss / Switzerland / Schweizer / Suisse / Helvetia / Eidgenössisch / Federal / Confédération — protected under Art. 960 OR and the Federal Act on the Protection of the Swiss Cross; requires prior consent of the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) or, for federal-authority wording, approval of the Federal Chancellery
Canton / cantonal or municipal heraldic elements and coats of arms — protected under cantonal emblem law; requires cantonal authorization

Crypto / Blockchain / Bitcoin / Digital Assets — not formally prohibited but treated as sensitive tokens triggering enhanced AML/CFT verification and a truthfulness-only acceptance; the applicant must prove the actual business scope to avoid misleading-name objections
Securities / Broker / Exchange — may imply regulated trading activity; requires confirmation that no FINMA securities-firm license is needed for the open-market wholesale brokerage model
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations in the Swiss commercial register system are granted for 30 days; an extension of an additional 30 days may be requested in writing before expiry, and a lapsed reservation releases the name for third parties. Upon a reservation rejection or a negative preliminary advice (negative Vorentscheid) by the cantonal commercial register office, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal commercial-register supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde über die Handelsregister / autorité de surveillance) within 30 days of notification, invoking incorrect legal assessment or incomplete factual examination of the name (analogous application of Art. 49 of the Federal Administrative Procedure Act, VwVG, SR 172.021). If the cantonal supervisory authority confirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) in St. Gallen within 30 days; further appeal to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) is limited to legal questions. Practical de-risking: submit up to three alternative names in priority order at the initial filing and obtain a written pre-clearance from the cantonal register office before notarizing the articles of association.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.additional_name_law_note: For the chosen business scope, a name such as 'CH_AG' or a descriptive German/English name mentioning 'Computer', 'Semiconductor', 'Server Components' or 'SSD' is acceptable; the name must not imply financial intermediation, investment advisory or regulated exchange activity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an Aktiengesellschaft engaged in wholesale brokerage of SSDs and server processors (ISIC 4651), a pure postal-only virtual office with mail forwarding and no physical access is NOT permissible as the sole registered seat. The Commercial Register Office requires a verifiable physical Swiss address at which the company's correspondence, accounting records and statutory files are kept and at which service of process can be effected. In practice, a physical business-center or co-working seat with a dedicated desk, locked file cabinet and a licensed local domicile representative is accepted and is materially indistinguishable from a conventional office for commercial-register purposes. The company must maintain actual administrative substance attributable to Switzerland, including Swiss-based bookkeeping, bank accounts and decision-making records, to avoid substance-assault challenges under the 2024 UBO-register enforcement policy and federal tax treaty anti-abuse rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: LOW-to-MEDIUM. The baseline probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office or the Cantonal Tax Administration is approximately 15% per 12-month cycle for a single-seat trading entity with a licensed domicile representative and complete digital accounting. The risk rises to approximately 45% if the entity shares a seat with three or more companies, maintains no staff or physical record presence, or transacts a high volume of Swift_TT wires with counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions. Entities registered in Zug, Geneva or Zurich with a 'substance-light' profile are the primary targets of the post-2024 UBO-register verification campaigns coordinated by the Federal Tax Administration and the Federal Office of Justice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_office_requirement_detail: Art. 613 OR requires the AG to have its seat in Switzerland; the registered office must be stated in the articles of association; any transfer of seat requires an amendment to the articles and re-registration with the competent cantonal commercial register office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Civil-law notary authentication of the deed of incorporation and Articles of Association (öffentliche Beurkundung der Statuten)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal civil-law notary public (Civil Law Notariat / Notaire public) in the canton of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff of the canton (e.g., Zurich/Zug notarial fee ordinances); progressive fee on the minimum share capital of CHF 100,000; prevailing range CHF 400 to 1,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Entry in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister / Registre du commerce) for the new AG
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office competent for the registered seat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal fee tariff (approx. CHF 300 to 600), abated for electronic filing through the cantonal e-register portal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / SHAB) statutory publication of the incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal publication authority — Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt), operated by the Federal Chancellery
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per publication block and per line (approx. CHF 55 per block); mandatory after commercial-register entry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and priority name-reservation request (Firmenreservation / Vorentscheid)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office via Zefix and the cantonal pre-clearance desk
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal fee of CHF 75 to 150 per reserved name; no separate federal fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO-register notification to the Swiss central beneficial-ownership register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Department of Finance (FDF) — Central UBO Register (Vedutenregister)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative charge of approx. CHF 50 under revised AMLA Art. 9j et seq.; notification mandatory upon registration in the Commercial Register

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille authentication package for five foreign originals (UBO passports, corporate register excerpts, certificates of good standing and bank reference letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal State Chancellery (competent apostille authority for foreign-origin documents) or Swiss embassy for consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document fee of CHF 40 to 60 under the Hague Apostille Convention implementation (SR 211.221.431); estimated five documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of UBO and director identity and corporate documents into an official Swiss language (German or French)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translation bureau (beeidigte Übersetzer / traducteurs assermentés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 200 to 400 per hour or flat fee per document; depends on the number of non-English documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial PEP/OFAC/UN/SECO sanctions screening database license — annual subscription for the entity and its officers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: KYC data provider (e.g., World-Check Refinitiv, Dow Jones, LexisNexis)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual subscription, medium-risk enhanced tier; volume-based pricing for a single entity with under 25 screened individuals

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical registered office and licensed local representative / domicile service — year 1
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss fiduciary company (SRO-supervised under AMLO, qualifying as a DNFBP)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 1,500 to 3,000 per year; higher in Zurich and Geneva; includes correspondence, record-keeping and statutory file access

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank verification of capital deposit and banker's attestation (Liberierungsbescheinigung)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or private bank holding the temporary incorporation account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank standard fee schedule of CHF 75 to 150 for the confirmation required under Art. 631 OR for the proof of payment of at least CHF 50,000 of the CHF 100,000 minimum capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External Swiss legal counsel — pre-incorporation due-diligence review, UBO piercing, name-clearance coordination and AML/CFT policy implementation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss law firm (corporate and AML/CFT practice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of CHF 350 to 550 per hour; fixed-fee engagement for a standard AG incorporation with one shareholder and one nominated director; includes drafting of articles, regulatory analysis and appeals preparedness

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, SR 220), Art. 626–642 (Aktiengesellschaft/SA); Art. 630 (Articles of Association); Art. 632 (Minimum capital); Art. 633 (Paid-up capital); Art. 640 (Registered office); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411), Art. 9–13
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Declaration of Incorporation together with Articles of Association (Statuten) filed electronically via the Central Company Name Index (ZEFIX)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The AG requires minimum share capital of CHF 100,000. At least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid up, but in aggregate no less than CHF 50,000 must be paid in cash. The paid-up amount must be deposited into a blocked Swiss bank account (Sperrkonto) held in escrow and may be used by the company only after the Commercial Register entry has been granted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors resolves: (1) The subscription of the Company's share capital of one thousand registered shares at CHF 100.00 each is ratified and full consideration of CHF 100,000 is confirmed deposited into a blocked account at a licensed bank. (2) The registered office is fixed at Zug, Switzerland, with the Commercial Register as the corresponding entry authority. (3) The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Chairperson with individual signature authority; [Name] as Chief Financial Officer and Secretary with joint signature authority; the employees shall be engaged in line with the approved payroll policy. (4) The Board commissions the notary to file the incorporation and further steps. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation of the Articles of Association and Declaration of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss notary public in the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators must appear before the notary with valid identification. The notary authenticates the Articles of Association, the subscription statement, the capital payment confirmation and the formal declaration of incorporation. The notarised deed, including the Statuten, is then transmitted electronically to the Commercial Register Office within 20 days.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or Swiss identity cards of all subscribers
Signed Articles of Association (Statuten)
Certificate of bank confirmation of capital payment (Sperrkonto)
Statement on non-cash contributions, if any
Draft public deed prepared by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, correct the articles and re-execute the deed with the same subscribers; amended pages must be initialled and re-signed before the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a blocked capital account and deposit the paid-up share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must open a corporate account in the company name with a FINMA-licensed bank. The full nominal amount of at least CHF 100,000 is deposited, and the bank issues a written confirmation stating the amount and blocking arrangement. Funds remain blocked until the Commercial Register entry is completed.
required_dossiers: Notarial draft of Articles of Association
List of subscribers and signatories
Source of funds declaration
Bank account opening forms and KYC documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, provide a supplementary bank statement, contract or affidavit within five business days; if the confirmation is stale, obtain an updated certificate from the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the commercial register application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the complete application for registration with the Commercial Register via the ZEFIX platform. The registrar checks legal compliance, capital payment confirmation, the formal articles, and the authority of the signatories. Upon approval, the entry is made and the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation
Bank confirmation of capital payment
Specimen signatures of directors and signatories
Declaration of the board regarding address and official service address
Application form signed by the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query, the notary must submit a supplementary written response or corrected deed within seven working days; any missing document must be delivered to the registry within that same period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official publication in the Swiss Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office for Buildings and Logistics (FOBL) / Commercial Register Publication System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the Commercial Register office automatically transmits the entry data for publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC). The publication includes the company name, registered office, statutory purpose, share capital, directors and signatory authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published content contains an error, file a written request with the Commercial Register office for a rectification publication; the correction is processed within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Federal Tax Administration and obtaining the UID/VAT number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company applies for a VAT number and the enterprise identification number (UID) through the ESTV's e-service portal or by paper form. VAT registration is mandatory if annual turnover exceeds CHF 250,000; voluntary registration may be obtained for wholesale traders importing goods. The code under ISIC 4651 is declared.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
Articles of Association
Statement of expected turnover
Bank account details
Completed application form (Form UID/VAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is deferred, correct the business activity description and turnover projection in the ESTV portal and provide a written explanation within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social insurance and occupational safety notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Compenswiss (Zentrale Ausgleichsstelle) and Cantonal Labour Inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must register as an employer with the Swiss compensation office for AHV/AVS and accident insurance. All employees are enrolled in the occupational pension fund and accident insurance. A business commencement notification is filed with the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate covering the premises and non-hazardous storage of electronic components.
required_dossiers: Company UID and Commercial Register extract
List of employees with social security numbers
Lease agreement or property title for the registered office/storage
Completed employer registration form (AHV)
Fire safety confirmation for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compensation office identifies incomplete data, submit the corrected employee register within five business days and pay any late registration fee; the labour inspectorate may issue a remediation order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalisation of corporate bank account and payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company completes the full account opening procedure using the registered articles and extract. The bank performs AML/KYC checks on ultimate beneficial owners. SWIFT TT payment capabilities and escrow-inspection wiring arrangements are configured according to the wholesale trading model.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Commercial Register extract
Articles of Association
UID confirmation
Declaration of beneficial ownership
Resolution of the board on signatory authorities
Completed bank account forms and AML questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AML compliance officer requests further information, deliver the beneficial ownership chart and source-of-wealth statements within 10 business days; consider applying for a pre-approved account opening interview at a Swiss private bank if the domestic bank refuses.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Department for Economy and Labour (Volkswirtschaftsdirektion Zug) – Business Commencement Notification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gewerbliche Meldung (Business Commencement Notification) – no specific industrial licence is required for wholesale trading of solid-state drives and server processors under Swiss SR 943.1

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Non-Industrial Wholesale: the activity does not meet any threshold under Annex 10 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVP/VOE, SR 814.011); no formal EIA report required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater discharge; applicable waste electrical and electronic equipment must be disposed via certified collection channels under VVEA (SR 814.611); packaging waste recovery obligations under the Ordinance on Packaging (SR 814.621); Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) limits do not apply as no manufacturing or coating activity exists.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Zug Fire Prevention Officer verifying smoke detection, escape routes and extinguisher placement; structural load inspection approval for the warehouse area from the Cantonal Building Inspectorate; workplace clearance from the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate confirming compliance with SUVA safety obligations and the Swiss Accident Prevention Ordinance (VUV, SR 832.30).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) - Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV); portal: https://www.esty.admin.ch/en
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must apply for a Swiss VAT number (MWST/TVA) via the FTA’s online VAT registration service. Requirements include proof of legal existence (e.g., extract from commercial register or equivalent foreign registration), a Swiss business address, and a declaration of actual or anticipated Swiss taxable turnover. An Aktiengesellschaft (AG) receives a nine-digit UID plus MWST/TVA suffix upon successful registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss tax law does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election; all Aktiengesellschaft (AG) entities are mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Available elections are limited to VAT grouping under Art. 17 of the Swiss VAT Act (eligible related entities may file as a single taxable person) and specific hybrid mismatch elections implemented to align with BEPS Action 2, such as the election to apply the transparency rule for in-scope hybrid instruments in accordance with the Swiss Dispossession Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual taxable turnover from supplies in Switzerland (Art. 10 VATA), inclusive of reductions; small businesses under this threshold are exempt but may opt for and remain liable to VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or continuous digital stamping is required under Swiss VAT law. However, all invoices (electronic or paper) must satisfy Art. 37 VATA content requirements. Export transactions require an electronic export declaration through the Swiss Customs Administration’s 'e-dec' system, which transmits customs data in near-real-time. Approved Exporter status permits simplified customs procedures but does not eliminate the obligation to file electronic customs declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export supplies of physical goods (including SSD and CPU chips) qualify for the 0% VAT rate when the supplier is the exporter or the goods are exported by a third party on the supplier’s behalf, and the goods are physically removed from the Swiss customs territory to a foreign destination. The recipient must be located outside Switzerland. For offshore services that are directly related to exported goods, zero-rating may apply provided the service is supplied to an overseas recipient and the connection to the exported goods is established.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: International Transport Document (Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill)
Proof of Foreign Customs Entry (if available)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) retains the right to reassess zero-rated supplies and retroactively claw back the corresponding input VAT deduction if export evidence is insufficient or fraudulent. The standard civil penalty for VAT evasion equals the evaded tax amount (Art. 66 VATA); aggravated cases are subject to criminal prosecution under Art. 72 VATA and the Swiss Penal Code, including custodial sentences, fines, and an extended five-year limitation period for reassessment. FTA audits scrutinise export documentation integrity, transport contracts, and payment cycles to detect fictitious exports or circular trading.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) acting as the central bank, and the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) overseeing financial market policy and cross-border capital movement reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under the broad freedom of the Code of Obligations and the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA). No general approval is required for foreign exchange operations, profit remittances, or cross-border capital flows. However, Swiss-domiciled entities must comply with balance-of-payments reporting to the SNB, and inbound/outbound transfers exceeding CHF 1 million are subject to monthly statistical disclosure. Dividends and profit repatriations are not subjected to exchange controls, but may trigger Swiss withholding tax at a statutory rate of 35%, with relief under applicable double taxation treaties. The Swiss franc is freely floating, and the SNB does not impose convertibility restrictions, surrender rules, or minimum holding periods, preserving high liquidity and capital mobility for the CH_AG wholesale semiconductor trading entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts in Switzerland. An entity is not required to surrender hard-currency export proceeds to the SNB, nor is there any obligation to convert export income into Swiss francs. Receipts from global SSD and CPU chip wholesale settlement may be held in foreign currency or repatriated freely. The only compliance duty is the SNB's Balance of Payments statistics reporting, which applies to each payment transaction individually or cumulatively exceeding CHF 1 million per month, requiring submission of the payment code and counterpart information in accordance with Annex 4 of the SNB reporting directives.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banca Stato (Cantonale Ticinese) – if operations expanded to Ticino

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Unregulated offshore digital EMIs cannot lawfully accept Swiss client deposits because deposit-taking requires a banking license under the Swiss Banking Act. A non-bank fintech may only act as a payment initiator or technical service provider if fully segregated from funds, and must hold a FinTech license from FINMA if obtaining deposits above CHF 1 million only for short periods, or operate under the Swiss Payment Services Act if not taking deposits. For cross-border settlement of semiconductor commodity trades, the only reliable payment service is a supervised licensed EMI or bank in Switzerland, or a European EMI passporting into Switzerland under the cross-border provision, but account opening with such EMIs is not equivalent to a domestic bank account for escrow or trade-dispute purposes. Therefore, for the target wholesale SSD/CPU chip trading entity, the recommended approach is a domestic Tier-1 bank account for all escrow-related transactions and a secondary licensed EMI for minor disbursements, subject to full KYC remittance checks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft engaged in international SSD and CPU wholesale trading, classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced, physical presence of the beneficial owner and at least one authorized signatory is generally mandatory at the account-opening KYC interview. UBS, Raiffeisen, and ZKB uniformly require either an in-person interview at a Swiss branch or a personal appearance before a Swiss consular officer or a notaire with apostille certification for remote verification. Relaxation is permitted only for recognized Swiss FINMA-regulated banks, e.g., UBS may accept a certified true passport copy notarized by a foreign bank in the same correspondent network, but the compliance team will likely impose a video call plus verifiable biometric at the Swiss Embassy. Fully remote account opening is not offered to a CH_AG engaged in IT hardware wholesale, due to the elevated Vendor Fraud and dual-use electronics concerns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction counterparties — shipping or invoicing to Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Syria, or entities in Digital Asset Sanctions lists, which are expressly prohibited for semiconductor products.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full compliance pack: (1) Export classification for each SSD/CPU (HS 8471.70.50 / 8542.31), (2) dual-use license from SECO if any end-application is industrial, telecom, or encryption, (3) end-user certificate (EUC), (4) signed no-embargo documentation from each buyer, and (5) system-generated negative screen against SDN lists, OFAC, and Swiss SECO embargo list, updated within 24 hours before payment acceptance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment risk — payment coming from unrelated beneficiary or not equal to the commercial invoice amount.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Retain of trade contract, proforma invoice, packing slip, customs declaration, full documentary chain, and a written affidavit from the overseas buyer confirming the payment is from its own treasury account; where third-party payment is unavoidable, obtain a written irrevocable instruction and complete the bank's Form N-2 disclosure within 48 hours.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated monthly turnover / particle of large cash-like transfers from shell finance structures or digital-asset intermediaries, which may activate enhanced due diligence and independent source-of-wealth review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce a board-approved treasury policy, audited financials, ledger of all trade receivables/payables, inventory transfer confirmations from bonded warehouses, and copy of directors' source of wealth declaration; submit bank statement showing purchase of goods from quarantined supply-chain finance facilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cyber-fraud and phishing loss occasioned by account takeover during escrow settlement of high-value electronics.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implementing contractual confirmation of payment instructions by a second channel, domain name security certificates, signed instruction authentication, and trade insurance recovery trail; if fraud occurs, submit initial incident report to police and the Swiss Banking Ombudsman annex memos, and provide full electronic log to the bank under the proactive loss-defense protocol.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from parent shareholders in Switzerland or foreign jurisdictions are performed via SWIFT MT103, using the Swiss purpose code 'D.III.1 – Capital contribution' (Einlage) in accordance with SNB Balance-of-Payments reporting. The bank will require an updated excerpt from the Commercial Register confirming the paid-in capital, a board resolution authorising the capital increase, and for injections originating from non-OECD jurisdictions, the bank requires a source-of-funds statement and a legal disclosure of the formal transfer trail to major shareholders. Transaction monitoring applies to the amount versus the bank-registered authorised share capital; for security-relevant goods trading, the capital account will be segregated into an escrow sub-ledger. All inbound capital flows should be booked with a clear payment reference quoting the share registry ID and the SNB payment code 'PL 103' if annual total exceeds CHF 1 million.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for SSD/CPU purchases and sales are executed predominantly over the SWIFT MT103 standard for direct telegraphic transfers and via SWIFT MT700 for documentary Letters of Credit covering consignment shipments. The treasury blueprint recommends: (1) domestic Taiwanese or Korean suppliers and customers concerned with Open Account terms mitigate the transaction by using a SWIFT MT103 with a matching inspect-and-pay condition embedded in the bank's collection service, (2) high-value shipments above CHF 500,000 are arranged under an Irrevocable Unconfirmed Commercial LC (sight) with a Swiss bank as issuing/advising bank, ensuring title transfer and compliance with the Incoterms 2020 shipment terms (FCA / CIF). For payment messaging, every outbound remittance must include the Swiss transaction code (e.g., 'T1' for import of goods, 'T2' for export of goods) and the business reference of the underlying purchase order. Settlement currency matching is recommended to be USD for global memory/chip trades and CHF or EUR for European counterparties, but SWIFT supports any freely convertible currency. The entity must maintain a dedicated liquidity ledger for LC margins and carry a reserve buffer of 7% of the outstanding LC balance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter forward foreign exchange contracts (US Dollar vs Swiss Franc, Euro vs Swiss Franc, US Dollar vs Euro) available from all Swiss banks with an ISDA Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in emerging market currencies such as Chinese Renminbi, South Korean Won, or Taiwanese Dollar, permitted when the underlying is a genuine trade payment obligation and the contract is for hedging only, not speculation
Cross-currency swaps for matching the USD and EUR working capital cycles, in particular converting (CHF vs USD) for fixed/floating payment streams
FX options (European style) as a bank-provided, permissible product to hedge anticipated trade flows pivot with the board-approved treasury policy
Marketable swaps via Swiss Debt Issuance and Structured Products with FINMA-regulated banks, subject to the eligible counterparty confirmation of IFRS 9 hedge accounting treatment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Commercial Register Details (Jahreserklärung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (per registered seat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after each financial year close (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to CHF 5,000 (approximately USD 5,750) per late filing; continued default may lead to strike-off and dissolution of the entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit required if two of three thresholds exceeded for two consecutive years: total assets > CHF 20 million; annual turnover > CHF 40 million; average employees > 250. Limited audit required if two thresholds exceeded: total assets > CHF 10 million; annual turnover > CHF 20 million; average employees > 50. Smaller companies may waive audit by unanimous shareholders' resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP according to the Code of Obligations (Art. 957-960d OR), optionally IFRS for certain regulated or listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership details filed in the commercial register must be reviewed and confirmed during the annual confirmation; any share transfers or UBO changes must be updated with the register before the annual confirmation submission.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: The statutory federal headline rate is 8.5% of taxable profit after federal corporate income tax. Cantonal and communal profit taxes vary by jurisdiction; for the Zug benchmark, the combined federal, cantonal, and communal effective ordinary rate is approximately 14.5% to 15.0% for a trading company.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland does not generally offer broad tax holidays for distribution/trading entities. Preferential tax status may be available under the Swiss patent box regime and R&D superdeduction, but these are inapplicable to a wholesale SSD/CPU distributor lacking qualifying IP. A cantonal holding/principal company structure may benefit from the participation deduction and notional interest deduction in certain cantons, reducing effective rates on qualifying dividend and capital gains income. For an active wholesale trading company, no material tax holiday applies; the effective rate remains the ordinary combined rate of approximately 15% in Zug.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal and cantonal combined corporate tax return, form 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales', filed electronically through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration’s eTax platform or the Zug cantonal tax portal (TaxMe / eTax Zug) using approved software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate tax return is due within six months after the close of the financial year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is 30 June of the following year. Extension requests may be granted by the competent cantonal authority, typically up to an additional three to six months, provided the request is timely filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification and general information: legal form, UID number, commercial register number, tax domicile, financial year, and activity code (ISIC/NOGA code).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Swiss AG's exact legal name, registered office, and UID. Non-resident shareholders are not named in this line; they are disclosed in the share register if required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of commercial balance sheet to taxable net profit: add non-deductible expenses (e.g., taxes on profit, board remuneration excess, unjustified expenses) and deduct tax-exempt income (e.g., participation income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident–owned AG, the commercial accounts must fully reflect arm's length transactions; any hidden profit distribution to shareholders must be reversed. Keep statutory books in accordance with Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 958 to 963.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of net profit before tax, as shown in the income statement under commercial accounting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident adjustments permitted in the local statutory accounts; all cross-border pricing adjustments are made via supplementary tax schedules, not by altering the income statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation deduction: reduction of income from qualifying substantial shareholdings in Swiss or foreign subsidiaries (minimum 10% of nominal capital or an acquisition cost of at least CHF 1 million and a holding period of at least 12 months).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG, not the foreign parent, claims this deduction. For a wholesale AG with no direct foreign investments, normally not applicable. If the AG owns a lower-tier holding, submit proof of qualifying participation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward deduction: offset of prior-year losses within the 7-year statutory period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses deductible only to the extent suffered and realized by the Swiss AG. No tax consolidation with foreign affiliates. Anti-abuse provisions restrict loss offset following an acquisition (Art. 58(1) DBG).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax reconciliation: inclusion of statutory tax statements (Form 108 and 110) confirming 35% Swiss withholding tax due on domestic dividends and other 35% taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company as debtor must withhold 35% on all distributions to shareholders. For non-resident shareholders applying treaty relief in advance, the FTA requires a refund procedure after the distribution is made, except where the simplified offset procedure is approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing annex and cross-border related-party transactions: disclosure of intercompany purchases, sales, financing, royalties, and allocation of profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss AG trading SSD/CPU chips as a limited-risk distributor or entrepreneurial broker, provide a concise TP summary and retain full Local File/Master File documentation for submission upon request (typically within 60 days).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 under cantonal law. If the return is not filed, the tax authority issues a default assessment, which may include a 10% to 30% surcharge. Interest on underpaid tax accrues at 3% per annum. Intentional tax evasion (Art. 174 DBG) triggers a fine of 40% to 100% of the tax evaded. Merely filing late without intent to evade may incur a fixed fine, but repeated non-compliance escalates to default assessment with surcharge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Swiss withholding tax on dividends is 35% of the gross distribution, levied on ordinary, bonus, and constructive dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To reduce the 35% Swiss withholding tax under a relevant double tax agreement, the non-resident shareholder must file Form 84/S (Refunds for Dividends, Interest, and Royalties) with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration, attaching the appropriate DTA residence certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority, evidence of beneficial ownership, and, where required, proof of shareholding percentage and holding period. For Hong Kong, a direct tax treaty with Switzerland exists, providing a reduced dividend withholding rate of 0% for a Hong Kong company holding at least 10% of the Swiss AG's share capital and where the investment exceeds CHF 200,000; for China, the treaty rate is 10% generally and 5% for a Chinese company holding at least 25% of the capital (subject to certain conditions); for Germany, the treaty rate is 15% generally and 0% for a qualifying parent company holding at least 10%; for the UK, 0% for a parent holding at least 10%. The FTA must be satisfied that the shareholder has substance and is the beneficial owner; mere treaty shopping is rejected. Submit the refund claim within three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss source interest paid to a non-resident is generally not subject to Swiss withholding tax unless paid on a Swiss domestic bond or bearier bond issued publicly; intercompany loans from a foreign parent to a Swiss borrower are typically free of Swiss WHT if structured as a genuine loan not evidenced by a bond. Royalties paid by a Swiss company to a non-resident are not subject to Swiss withholding tax. Under applicable DTAs, treaty rates for interest and royalties vary: for interest paid under the Swiss–Hong Kong DTA, the rate is 0% (no source tax) for interest beneficially owned by a Hong Kong enterprise; for Swiss–China DTA, interest rate is 10%, royalties 10%; for Swiss–Germany DTA, interest is 0% if beneficially owned by an enterprise, royalties 0% generally (except certain copyright royalties); for Swiss–UK DTA, interest 0%, royalties 0%. However, because Switzerland does not impose WHT on cross-border interest and royalties from ordinary intercompany arrangements, no actual Swiss source tax is due; the foreign recipient remains taxable in its residence jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File / Master File) is required for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding CHF 500,000 in intercompany turnover or where the Swiss entity's annual turnover exceeds CHF 10 million. For a high-volume wholesale SSD/CPU trading entity, these thresholds are generally exceeded; therefore, contemporaneous TP documentation must be maintained and filed upon request. A Swiss Taxpayer Accuracy Spec sheet (Annex TP-4) may be required by the Zug tax administration.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) for commodity-like SSD/CPU chips based on market quotations
Resale Price Method for routine distributor functions
Cost Plus Method for logistics or assembly activities
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) for limited-risk distribution
Profit Split Method for integrated supply-chain functions with unique intangibles
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Swiss law does not apply offshore ESR regimes, but domestic substance requirements derive from the legal-economic approach: a corporation must have independent substance to be treated as the taxpayer for the assets and income it reports. The company must have an actual seat and place of management, bank accounts, qualified personnel, administrative facilities, books and records, minutes of shareholder and board meetings held in Switzerland, and actual decision-making in Switzerland. For a Zug AG engaged in wholesale SSD/CPU trading, substance should cover: local directors, a physical office, sufficient commercial activity, bookkeeping, foreign bank accounts, and negotiation/logistics roles. If substance is deficient, the tax authority may reclassify the entity as a mere agent or conduit, attribute income to the effective entrepreneur, and deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a knowingly incomplete or false tax return, maintaining dual books, understating gross turnover from wholesale transactions of SSD/CPU chips, or failing to declare taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 174 DBG: fine of 40% to 100% of the evaded tax. Art. 175 DBG: tax fraud by using false documents or falsified accounts carries a fine of up to 2.5 times the evaded tax, and if committed through criminal means, imprisonment under Art. 146 StGB up to 5 years. The tax re-assessment is payable with interest at 3% per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately file false returns may be personally criminally liable. They face a fine and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. Under civil law, they owe the company restitution for the tax loss under Art. 754 CO if their conduct was unlawful and blameworthy. In severe cases, travel bans and extradition may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham / Shell company without economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Zug AG that lacks genuine business operations, employees, office, and decision-making, while recording trading income that in fact belongs to a foreign parent or offshore affiliate, for the purpose of obtaining Swiss tax residence and treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority disregards the substanceless entity for tax purposes and reattributes the income to the effective management jurisdiction. Additional assessments are raised with interest. A hidden distribution of profits may be deemed, triggering 35% Swiss withholding tax. Fines up to 2.5 times the tax evaded apply. Treaty benefits are denied. The company may be struck off by the commercial register if it fails to meet substance requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for intentional establishment and operation of a sham entity under Art. 754 CO. They may be sued by the tax authority in bankruptcy for tax deficiencies if they acted grossly negligently. Prison sentences of up to 5 years can be imposed if they personally participated in fraudulent documentation. Travel bans under stock exchange or tax investigation proceedings are possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Brokering or facilitating sales of SSD/CPU chips to sanctioned entities, using shell counterparties, accepting funds from unclear sources, or engaging in reverse invoicing to launder proceeds. Failure to perform adequate KYC/CDD checks on foreign buyers (especially from high-risk jurisdictions) despite red flags.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Swiss AML (GwSG) due diligence may result in a fine of up to CHF 500,000. Money laundering under Art. 305bis StGB carries imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine. Breach of Swiss embargo and sanctions regulations (e.g., goods destined for Iran, Syria, Russia) is punishable by imprisonment of up to 10 years and a fine. Confiscation of proceeds and criminal liability for the beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute sanction-affected trades are personally liable. They face criminal imprisonment, personal fines, and extradition risk. Asset freezes and travel bans are commonly imposed. The director's personal assets can be seized to cover restitution for non-financial loss or fines. The corporate veil will not shield deliberate criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing documentation failure and transfer mispricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain comprehensive TP documentation, applying non-arm's length pricing to intra-group wholesale SSD/CPU trades, allocating an excessive share of profit to a low-tax foreign entity, or not cooperating with the tax authority's documentation requests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 58 DBG gives the FTA power to adjust profits to arm's length. Implicit penalty: burden of proof shifts to taxpayer if documentation missing. Deficiency assessments plus interest (3%) apply. Intentional under-taxation may produce a fine of 40%–100% of the evaded tax. Non-procedural failure can be fined up to CHF 10,000. Foreign exchange adjustments and recalculation of deemed dividends may trigger withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false TP documentation or knowingly approve artificial pricing can be criminally prosecuted for tax fraud under Art. 175 DBG. They are personally and jointly liable for the company's tax damage under Art. 754 CO. In cross-border cases, Swiss authorities may cooperate via mutual assistance leading to personal seizure and extradition. Imprisonment up to 5 years possible if the misconduct constitutes ordinary criminal fraud.
